operations.specification: Implement guest registration/join by validating the submitted guest credentials and establishing a new authenticated session for the visitor. The service must create or associate the guest identity according to the join workflow, then issue fresh access and refresh tokens in the authorized response. Enforce input validation, reject duplicate or invalid join attempts, and return a clear authentication error when the join request cannot be completed.
operations.description:
Creates a guest authorization session for an unauthenticated visitor who is joining the platform. This endpoint is part of the authentication flow for temporary visitors and returns the authorized token bundle needed to continue using the API.

The operation is public and does not require an existing authenticated actor. It should validate the join payload and, on success, issue the standard authorized response described by the `IErpHrmTimeGuest.IAuthorized` contract. Any invalid registration or join attempt must fail with an authentication error rather than creating a partial session.

This endpoint is intended to support the guest actor workflow only. It does not perform login for existing member accounts, and it should not expose organization-scoped data until a valid organization context is established through later business operations.

requestBody.description: Guest join request payload used to create or activate a guest authorization session.

responseBody.description: Authorized token response returned after a successful guest join.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Implement refresh-token exchange for guest sessions by validating the incoming refresh token, verifying that it is still active and unexpired, and issuing a new authorized token bundle. Reject expired, revoked, malformed, or replayed refresh tokens. If the refresh token cannot be trusted, return an authentication error and do not issue new credentials.
operations.description:
Renews the authorization state for a guest session using a refresh token. This endpoint is public and exists so a guest can continue an active authorization session without re-running the join flow.

On success, the service returns the standard `IErpHrmTimeGuest.IAuthorized` token bundle. The refresh operation must validate the supplied refresh token carefully and must refuse to issue new credentials when the token is expired, invalid, or otherwise unusable.

This endpoint is part of the guest authentication lifecycle only. It does not require a logged-in member, and it should not be used to switch organization context or access business data directly.

requestBody.description: Guest refresh request payload containing the refresh token to exchange for a new authorized session.

responseBody.description: Authorized token response returned after a successful guest token refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Implement member registration by validating the submitted email and password, creating the member account, and issuing the initial authenticated token set in a single transaction. Check for duplicate email addresses before insertion and reject already-registered emails with a conflict error. If account creation must also initialize session state or profile linkage, do so only after the member row is successfully created. Return a JWT authorization payload containing the access token, refresh token, and any standard expiration metadata expected by IErpHrmTimeMember.IAuthorized. Ensure password handling uses secure hashing and never persists plaintext credentials.
operations.description:
Registers a new member account for the ERP HRM and time tracking platform. The operation creates the authenticated user record identified by the member actor and returns the authorization payload needed to start using the system.

This endpoint is the entry point for users who are joining the platform with email and password credentials. It is part of the authentication flow that precedes organization-scoped actions such as switching into a tenant context, managing organization memberships, or using time tracking features.

If the submitted email is already in use, the operation must fail with a conflict-style error. Validation errors for malformed email or weak passwords should be returned clearly so clients can correct the request before retrying.

requestBody.description: Registration payload for creating a new member account with email and password credentials.

responseBody.description: Authorization payload returned after successful member registration, including tokens required for authenticated access.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate an existing member using email and password credentials. Look up the member record by email, verify the password hash, and reject invalid credentials with an unauthorized error. On success, issue a fresh authorization payload suitable for authenticated API calls. If the system tracks member sessions, record the login event for security auditing, but do not require any organization context at this stage. Never reveal whether the email exists versus the password being wrong; return the same generic authentication failure for both cases.
operations.description:
Logs an existing member into the ERP HRM and time tracking platform using email and password credentials. The operation validates identity and returns the authenticated token bundle used for subsequent requests.

This endpoint is for returning users who already have a member account. After successful login, the client can select or switch organization context and then access organization-scoped resources such as employees, projects, timesheets, and reports.

Invalid credentials must be rejected without disclosing whether the email address is unknown or the password is incorrect. This protects account privacy and reduces information leakage.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for an existing member account.

responseBody.description: Authorization payload returned after successful member login, including tokens required for authenticated access.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate the refresh token, confirm it has not expired or been revoked, and issue a new authorization payload. Rotate refresh tokens if the implementation supports rotation, and reject reused or invalid tokens with an unauthorized error. This endpoint should not require email or password verification because its purpose is to renew an existing authenticated session. Keep token parsing strict and ensure the refresh token is bound to the same member identity that originally received it.
operations.description:
Renews an existing member session by exchanging a valid refresh token for a new authorization payload. This keeps the member signed in without requiring the email and password to be entered again.

The endpoint is part of the standard JWT session lifecycle for authenticated members. It supports continued access to organization-scoped resources such as employee management, time tracking, and reporting while preserving security through token expiration and renewal.

Expired, malformed, revoked, or otherwise invalid refresh tokens must be rejected. The response should only be produced when the token is valid and the member identity can be safely re-established.

requestBody.description: Refresh token payload used to obtain a renewed authorization bundle.

responseBody.description: Authorization payload returned after successful token refresh, including the renewed access credentials.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of member sessions for the currently authenticated account.

This operation exposes issued session records so a member can review active and recent login activity, including client context such as IP address, the entry URL, and the referrer captured at session creation or refresh time. The data comes directly from the member session store and is intended for security visibility and account management.

Results are always scoped to the authenticated member and must never return another member's sessions. The response supports filtering, pagination, and sorting so consumers can build session history views and security screens. If the request contains invalid pagination or sort values, the service must reject the request with a validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_member_sessions for the authenticated member only.
Filter by the current member identity from the auth context; do not accept a member identifier in the body because the caller must only see their own records.
Support search against ip, href, and referrer, plus date-range filters on created_at and expired_at. Support sorting by created_at and expired_at, defaulting to newest sessions first.
Apply pagination with page and limit fields, and return total count plus items in a paginated envelope.
Enforce that expired sessions remain visible if requested by filters; do not mutate or revoke data from this endpoint.
If the auth context is missing or invalid, return an unauthorized error. If filters are malformed or sorting references unsupported fields, return a validation error.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the authenticated member's session summaries.

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for the current member's session list.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single stored member session record by identifier.

This operation returns one authenticated member session record from the member session table, which is used to keep track of login activity and security-related session context. It is intended for session inspection and administrative or user-facing security workflows that need to view one session at a time.

The record belongs to a member account and should be read in the context of the current authenticated user and the platform's access rules. If the session does not exist, the API should return a not-found response. If the caller is not allowed to view the session, the API should return a forbidden response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load one row from erp_hrm_time_member_sessions by id. Verify the session exists before returning it. Return the full session entity fields only: id, erp_hrm_time_member_id, ip, href, referrer, created_at, and expired_at. Do not infer any additional session metadata.

Enforce authorization so the current authenticated member can only read their own session unless a higher-privileged account/session administration rule is explicitly applied elsewhere in the system. If the session does not belong to the current member and no elevated permission exists, return forbidden. If the row is missing, return not found.

Because the schema shows only a child relation to member, avoid joining unrelated tables unless required to hydrate the response contract. Keep the implementation read-only and use the session primary key lookup as the main query.

responseBody.description: A single member session record with its stored session metadata.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the member session to retrieve (UUID).
parameters.name: sessionId

operations.description:
Search password reset requests for member accounts.

This operation returns a paginated list of password reset records stored in the member password reset table. Each record represents a reset token issued for a specific member account and includes its expiration and consumption state so support and security workflows can inspect active, expired, or already-used reset requests.

The search results are scoped to the authenticated caller's permitted access to member security data. Implement filtering by member account, token, usage status, and creation or expiration ranges, and support pagination and sorting for administrative review and troubleshooting. Invalid or expired tokens must not be exposed beyond their summary metadata.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_member_password_resets with pagination, sorting, and filters.
Support filters for member ID, token lookup, consumption status (unused/used/expired), created-at range, and expires-at range.
Join to erp_hrm_time_members only when needed to display member identity fields in the summary projection; do not expose password hashes.
Respect authorization so only privileged callers can search reset records.
Order results by newest first by default, and return total count plus page metadata.
Treat deleted_at as excluded records unless the implementation explicitly includes revoked history; if included, make that behavior explicit in the query contract and keep summaries consistent.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member password reset summaries.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination options for member password reset records.

operations.description:
Retrieve a password reset request record by its identifier.

This operation returns the password reset entry associated with a member account, including the reset token, expiration time, and whether the token has already been consumed. It is intended for the password recovery workflow and for validating the current state of a reset request before allowing a password update.

The record is linked to a member account through the member relationship, and the identifier in the path refers to the password reset record itself. Consumers should use the returned expiration and consumed timestamps to determine whether the reset request is still usable. If the record does not exist or has been removed, the request must fail with a not-found error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load a single erp_hrm_time_member_password_resets row by its primary key id.
Join nothing else unless needed for response projection, but ensure the associated member relation is available if the response schema requires it. Validate that the record exists and is not deleted_at-marked when the service treats deleted rows as inaccessible.

Return the full password reset entity with token, expires_at, used_at, created_at, and updated_at. Do not accept a request body. If no row matches the provided resetId, raise a not-found error. If the row is expired or already used, still return the record for inspection unless the higher-level password reset workflow requires rejection; this endpoint is read-only and should not mutate state.

responseBody.description: The password reset request record identified by the provided reset ID.

parameters.description: Password reset record identifier (UUID).
parameters.name: resetId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of member email verification records.

This operation is used to inspect email verification token records that belong to a member account. It supports browsing verification issuance history, expiration state, and whether a verification token has already been consumed for confirmation.

The results are intended for account and verification management workflows, so the response should expose summary information only and must not return the raw token value. Access must remain scoped to the authenticated member and any server-side authorization rules for account security.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_member_email_verifications with pagination, filtering, and sorting.
Filter by member identity, verification state, expiration state, deletion state, and creation/expiration time ranges as supported by the request schema.
Return summary rows ordered by the requested sort; default to newest first using created_at descending.
Never expose the token string in the list response. When a record is marked verified, include verified_at in the summary. Respect deleted_at if the implementation supports browsing revoked records, otherwise exclude deleted rows by default.
Enforce that only the authenticated member or authorized account-management workflow can access records for the relevant member.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of member email verification summaries.

requestBody.description: Pagination, filtering, and sorting criteria for member email verification records.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single member email verification record.

This operation returns the verification token record issued for a member account so clients can inspect its lifecycle state, including when it was created, when it expires, and whether it has already been verified or revoked. The record belongs to one member account and is used by the platform to confirm ownership of a member email address during account activation and related verification workflows.

The response includes the token metadata needed to determine whether the verification link is still usable, already consumed, or no longer valid. If the requested record does not exist or the caller is not allowed to access the member-scoped verification record, the request must be rejected with the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load a single row from erp_hrm_time_member_email_verifications by id using the UUID path parameter.
Join or hydrate the owning member relation only if the platform's standard detail response requires it; otherwise return the record fields directly from the verification table.
Validate that the record exists and is not outside access scope. Because this entity is tied to a member account, enforce authentication/authorization rules before returning it.
Do not accept a request body. Handle missing records with a not-found response.
Preserve the exact persisted timestamps and token value; do not derive or mutate lifecycle values in this operation.

responseBody.description: Full member email verification record including lifecycle timestamps and ownership reference.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the email verification record (UUID primary key).
parameters.name: verificationId

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member’s shared global profile.

This operation changes the profile information stored on the member account itself, including the display name, avatar image, and phone number. These values are shared across all organizations the member belongs to, so the update is reflected everywhere the account appears in the platform.

The update applies only to the single global profile record associated with the authenticated member. It does not create organization-specific profile data, and it must preserve the member’s account identity, credentials, and organization memberships. Validation errors should be returned when submitted values do not meet profile constraints or when the request attempts to treat shared profile data as tenant-specific.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member from the current security context and load the single shared profile record from erp_hrm_time_members.
Update only the profile columns supported by the schema: display_name, avatar_image_url, and phone_number. Do not update email, password_hash, or any organization-related records.

Apply a transaction-safe row update with optimistic concurrency if supported by the service layer. Persist updated_at with the current timestamp. If the avatar URL is provided, validate it as a URI/URL string; if phone number is provided, validate it as a plain optional string; display name must be present and non-empty according to profile rules.

Reject requests that attempt to scope the profile to a specific organization or include unsupported fields. Return 401 when the user is not authenticated. Return 403 only if the authenticated principal is not allowed to access the member profile endpoint. Return validation errors for malformed profile data.

responseBody.description: The updated authenticated member profile with the shared global profile fields.

requestBody.description: Profile fields to update for the authenticated member’s shared global profile.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of organizations available in the current account context.

This operation is used to browse organization records and locate tenant entries by name, status, and creation range. It is intended for multi-organization workflows where a member may need to review the organizations they own or belong to, and for administrative interfaces that need searchable organization lists.

The result reflects the organization tenant record defined by the organization table, including its identity, ownership, lifecycle state, and profile fields such as description and logo image URL. Organization-specific settings such as currency, timezone, and fiscal start month are maintained in the related settings record and may be projected into summaries when needed for list displays.

Use this endpoint with pagination and sorting to support UI browsing. If the request does not match an accessible organization scope, the service should return an empty page rather than exposing unrelated tenants. Invalid filters or unsupported sort fields should produce a validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the organization table as a paginated search endpoint.
Apply filters for organization name, status, and created-at range when supplied by the request body.
Support sorting by allowed organization fields, and always paginate the result set to prevent unbounded reads.
Join organization settings only when needed for summary projection; do not require settings rows for the base list query because the organization root record is the primary source of identity and lifecycle data.
Enforce tenant visibility rules from the authenticated member context if the application layer restricts organization browsing to owned or accessible organizations.
Return summary objects optimized for list rendering, including only the fields required by the consumer. If no records match, return an empty page.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization summaries.

requestBody.description: Search, pagination, and sorting criteria for organizations.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full organization record for the selected tenant.

This operation returns the organization identity and lifecycle data stored in the organization table, including the owner member reference, display name, optional description, optional logo image URL, status, and audit timestamps. It is intended for authenticated members who are already operating within an organization-scoped session and need to inspect the currently selected organization or a specific organization they are permitted to access.

The organization is the root boundary for tenant-isolated data, so this response represents only one organization record and does not include employees, projects, departments, or other related collections. If the organization does not exist or the caller is not allowed to access it in the current organization context, the request must fail with the appropriate not-found or authorization error.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the organization row by its UUID primary key.
Join the owner member relation only if the response schema requires owner details; otherwise return the organization entity fields directly.
Enforce organization-scoped authorization so the caller can only read organizations they are permitted to access.
Validate that the path parameter is a UUID and return a not-found error when no record exists.
Do not expose records from other organizations or infer related tenant data in this endpoint.
Preserve the database values for status and timestamps without transformation.

responseBody.description: The full organization record.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization to retrieve (UUID).
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Update an organization's profile and tenant settings.

This operation lets an organization owner change the organization's display name, description, and logo image, together with the operating settings that define how the tenant behaves across the platform. The organization record is the root tenant boundary, while its settings record stores currency, timezone, and fiscal start month as a dependent 1:1 extension.

Changes apply only to the organization identified by the path parameter and must not affect other organizations. The service must verify that the caller has permission to manage the selected organization and must preserve ownership, lifecycle state, and audit timestamps. Invalid organization references, unauthorized access, or invalid configuration values should be rejected with a validation or authorization error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the organization by id and ensure it belongs to the caller's authorized organization scope. Enforce that only organization owners or members with organization management permission can update it.

Update the organization root fields name, description, and logo_image_url only. Do not allow changes to owner_member_id, status, created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at from this endpoint.

Update the dependent organization settings row through the unique organization id relation. Editable settings fields are currency_code, timezone, and fiscal_start_month. Preserve the one-to-one relationship and use a single transaction so root and settings changes remain consistent.

Validate that name is not empty, logo_image_url is a valid URI when provided, currency_code and timezone are valid platform values, and fiscal_start_month is a 1-based month value. If the organization settings row is unexpectedly missing, either create it within the same transaction if the domain allows initialization here, or return a not-found/domain error consistent with the service rules.

Return the updated organization aggregate including its settings. If the organization does not exist, return 404. If the caller lacks access, return 403. If any editable value fails validation, return 400 with field-level errors.

responseBody.description: The updated organization record including its dependent settings.

parameters.description: The organization identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Editable organization profile and tenant settings values.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes an organization and all organization-owned operational data.

This operation is available only to an organization owner in the current organization context. Before deletion can proceed, the system must verify that every pending timesheet for the organization has been resolved and that there are no active employee contracts remaining. These rules protect unresolved work records and ongoing employment arrangements from being removed prematurely.

When deletion succeeds, the organization’s employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets are permanently removed from the system. The owner’s account remains available, but it is no longer associated with the deleted organization. Because organization data is owned by the tenant, this operation affects only the specified organization and does not impact any other organizations the requester may belong to.

If the organization does not exist, the requester is not authorized, the organization is not deletable due to unresolved timesheets or active contracts, or the current account violates ownership constraints, the service must reject the request with an appropriate validation or domain error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the organization by organizationId within the active request context and verify that the caller has organization-owner authority for that organization. Confirm that the organization belongs to the current tenant context and that the request is not attempting cross-tenant deletion.

Before deletion, validate the business prerequisites: all pending timesheets must be resolved, and there must be no active employee contracts. Also verify ownership constraints for the caller; if the caller is the sole owner, the deletion must be rejected unless ownership has already been transferred or the organization is being deleted through an allowed organization-deletion flow.

Execute deletion in a transaction. Remove organization-owned data in the required cascading order so that employees, projects, tasks, timelogs, and timesheets are permanently deleted with no recovery path in this specification. Ensure any related membership links and organization settings are removed consistently as part of the same atomic operation. Return the deleted organization payload if the backend supports returning the removed entity; otherwise return no body.

Map missing organization to not-found, ownership or permission failures to forbidden, and unresolved business prerequisites to a domain validation error explaining that pending timesheets or active contracts block deletion.

parameters.description: The identifier of the organization to delete in the current tenant scope.
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Retrieve the configuration record that defines an organization’s business operating context.

This endpoint returns the organization settings associated with the specified organization, including the ISO currency code, IANA timezone, and fiscal start month. These values are maintained as part of the organization profile and are used to interpret dates, reporting periods, and monetary display throughout the tenant.

The settings belong to a single organization and are resolved through the organization context provided in the path. If the organization does not exist, does not have settings, or the caller is not allowed to view that organization’s data, the request must be rejected. The response is intended for organization profile screens and other organization-scoped consumers that need the current operating context.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the organization by id and verify the caller is allowed to access that organization context before reading settings.
Fetch the single settings row via the unique organization foreign key on erp_hrm_time_organization_settings. If no settings row exists, return a not-found response rather than fabricating defaults.
Do not join unrelated tenant data. Return only the settings fields defined by the schema: id, organization reference, currency code, timezone, fiscal start month, and timestamps. Enforce organization isolation so the settings of any other organization are inaccessible. For unauthorized access or missing organization context, reject the request with the appropriate authorization or not-found error.

responseBody.description: The organization settings record for the requested organization.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization whose settings should be retrieved.
parameters.name: organizationId

operations.description:
Update the organization settings for a single tenant.

This operation lets the organization owner maintain the settings record that defines the organization’s operating context, including currency, timezone, and fiscal start month. These values are part of the organization profile and must apply only to the specified organization.

The service must verify that the authenticated member is the owner of the organization identified by `organizationId`, that the organization context is valid, and that the settings row belongs to the same organization. If the settings record does not exist, the implementation may create it only when the domain rules permit initial settings provisioning; otherwise it must return a not-found or conflict error according to the service conventions. Validation must ensure the currency code and timezone are acceptable platform values and the fiscal start month is a valid 1-based calendar month.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the organization by id and confirm it belongs to the current tenant context. Verify the authenticated user is the organization owner before allowing any write.

Fetch the unique settings row by erp_hrm_time_organization_id. Update only currency_code, timezone, and fiscal_start_month. Preserve immutable identifiers and timestamps. If the organization has no settings row and the business layer expects one to exist, surface a domain error rather than silently creating inconsistent data.

Validate that fiscal_start_month is an integer from 1 to 12, timezone is a valid IANA identifier, and currency_code is an accepted ISO currency code. Ensure the target organization matches the selected organization context and reject cross-organization access.

Return the updated settings entity after persistence. If authorization fails, return forbidden. If the organization does not exist or is not accessible, return not found. If input values fail validation, return a validation error.

responseBody.description: The updated organization settings record for the selected organization.

parameters.description: The organization identifier in the current organization context.
parameters.name: organizationId

requestBody.description: Values to update the organization's currency, timezone, and fiscal year starting month.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of organization memberships within the active organization context.

This operation exposes the membership links between member accounts and organizations, including each membership's status and whether it is the currently selected organization context. It is intended for organization-scoped browsing and administration, where the active organization determines which memberships are visible and actionable.

The list is filtered and sorted within the current organization boundary. Consumers can use it to inspect which members belong to the organization and how their membership context is currently configured. Because membership access is organization-specific, results must never cross into another organization's data.

Validation and authorization errors should be returned when the requester does not have permission to view membership data or when the selected organization context is missing or inconsistent with the active membership scope.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_organization_memberships using the active organization context as the primary scope. Filter by erp_hrm_time_organization_id from the current selected organization, and optionally filter by erp_hrm_time_member_id, status, and is_selected_context. Support pagination, search, and sorting in the request body; sorting should be applied on allowed columns such as created_at, updated_at, status, and is_selected_context.

Return only memberships visible in the current organization. Use joins to member and organization only if needed for downstream summary composition, but do not expose fields beyond the membership summary contract. Respect the unique membership constraint on (erp_hrm_time_member_id, erp_hrm_time_organization_id). Exclude logically deleted records by default unless the request explicitly asks for deleted items and the caller is authorized for administrative recovery workflows.

If the selected organization context is absent or does not match the membership scope, reject the request as a context error. If the caller lacks organization-scoped membership access, return a forbidden error. Ensure the response shape is a paginated summary collection suitable for list screens.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization membership summaries within the active organization context.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for organization memberships.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single organization membership record.

This endpoint returns the organization membership that links a member account to an organization, including the membership status and whether the membership is the currently selected organization context. It is used to inspect the access-scoped relationship between a user account and an organization without exposing unrelated organizations or other members' data.

The membership record belongs to exactly one member account and exactly one organization, and the lookup must respect the caller's current organization scope. If the requested membership does not exist, is outside the active organization context, or has been removed, the service must return a not-found response. Access should be restricted to authenticated members with permission to view organization membership data in the selected organization.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the organization membership by UUID from erp_hrm_time_organization_memberships with its related member and organization references if needed by the response mapper. Enforce organization context: the resolved membership must belong to the caller's selected organization and must not be deleted. Use the primary key lookup first, then verify the record's organization matches the active organization context before returning it. If the record is missing, deleted, or context-mismatched, return not found.

Do not infer role assignment fields because they are not present in this schema. Return only the membership entity shape that is supported by the loaded schema and the shared DTO conventions for this service. The accessor must remain unique under the organizationMemberships namespace.

responseBody.description: A single organization membership record including its organization-scoped status and context selection state.

parameters.description: Organization membership identifier (UUID) in the current organization scope.
parameters.name: organizationMembershipId

operations.description:
Create a new organization membership for an account within the currently selected organization.

This operation links a member account to an organization and establishes the organization-scoped access context for that person. It is used when an existing account is added to an organization or when a pending invitation is converted into an active membership. The membership record stores the member reference, organization reference, status, and whether the membership is the selected organization context for the member.

The service must enforce that the same member cannot be added to the same organization more than once, and it must resolve the target organization from the current organization context. If the member already belongs to other organizations, those memberships remain unchanged because access is always evaluated per organization membership.

Validation and persistence errors should be surfaced when the referenced member or organization does not exist, when the membership already exists, or when the caller lacks the required organizational authority to create memberships in the selected organization.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the organization from the active organization context and verify the caller has permission to add memberships in that organization. Validate that the target member exists and that no active or existing membership already links the same member and organization pair, using the unique constraint on (erp_hrm_time_member_id, erp_hrm_time_organization_id).

Create a new organization membership row with the provided member reference and organization reference, then set the membership status according to the business flow used by invitations or direct additions. Persist is_selected_context according to the service rule for the current organization context, ensuring only the intended membership becomes active in the selected organization scope.

Use a transaction if any related updates are required to normalize selected-context state. Reject attempts to create duplicate memberships with a conflict error, and reject missing member or organization references with not-found errors. Do not expose or accept system-managed fields such as id, created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at in the request body.

responseBody.description: The newly created organization membership.

requestBody.description: Data required to create an organization membership for an existing member account.

operations.description:
Update an organization membership record within the current organization scope.

This operation modifies the membership status and selected-context flag for a member account linked to an organization. An organization membership is the access link that determines which organization the member is currently working in, so changes here immediately affect organization-scoped access and context selection.

The membership record belongs to exactly one member and one organization, and those relationships are fixed by the existing record. Only the membership status and the selected-context flag may be updated through this endpoint. If the selected-context flag is changed, the service must ensure the member’s organization context remains consistent with the active membership rules used throughout the platform.

The service must validate that the membership exists, belongs to the current organization scope, and has not been removed. It should reject attempts to modify immutable identity fields or to apply changes that would violate the one-membership-per-member-and-organization constraint. If the update cannot be applied because the membership is missing or inaccessible in the current organization context, return the appropriate not-found or forbidden error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the membership by UUID and enforce organization-context access before any update. Do not allow changing erp_hrm_time_member_id or erp_hrm_time_organization_id because the endpoint is for updating the existing membership record only.

Update only status and is_selected_context from the request body. Persist updated_at automatically. If is_selected_context is set to true, ensure the selected membership behavior remains coherent for the member within the organization context; if the domain rules require a single selected membership per member, clear other selected memberships for the same member in the same organization scope within the same transaction.

Validate that the membership exists and is not deleted. If the current context does not match the membership organization, reject with forbidden or not found according to the service's access policy. Preserve referential integrity with member and organization relations. Return the updated membership record after commit.

responseBody.description: The updated organization membership record.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization membership to update.
parameters.name: organizationMembershipId

requestBody.description: Fields used to update the membership status and selected organization context flag.

operations.description:
Remove a member’s association with the current organization.

This operation deletes the organization membership record identified by the path parameter. Organization memberships define which users can access a tenant and which organization context is active for the member, so the deletion must be performed only within the currently selected organization and only by an authorized actor.

The membership removal affects access control for the target user in that organization, but it does not delete the underlying user account. Related organization-scoped data remains governed by the broader account and organization lifecycle rules, including employee deactivation behavior where applicable.

If the membership does not belong to the current organization, does not exist, or the caller lacks permission to manage members, the request must fail with an appropriate authorization or not-found error. The endpoint should also protect against removing the last remaining owner membership when that would violate organization ownership rules.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the organization membership by organizationMembershipId and verify it belongs to the authenticated user’s current organization context. Enforce permission checks so only callers with membership-management authority in the organization can delete the record.

Before deletion, validate business rules that prevent removing memberships needed to preserve organization ownership integrity. If the membership corresponds to the sole owner relationship for the organization, reject the request and instruct the caller to transfer ownership or delete the organization first.

Perform the deletion in a transaction. If the domain model requires side effects, ensure any membership-linked selection state is cleared for the affected member and that downstream access checks no longer treat the user as part of the organization. Do not delete the user account itself.

Return 404 when the membership does not exist in the current scope, 403 when the caller lacks rights, and a conflict-style error when ownership constraints prevent deletion. No response body is required on success.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the organization membership to remove within the current organization context.
parameters.name: organizationMembershipId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of employees for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint supports browsing employees by name, department, employment type, and status so organization members can understand how staff are grouped and managed within the tenant. Each result represents an employee record scoped to the active organization context and reflects the employee's current role, department assignment, position title, employment type, and status.

Access is limited to users with employee-view permission in the selected organization. Search, filtering, and pagination apply only to the active organization context, and the response must never include employees from other organizations.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query erp_hrm_time_employees for the active organization context only. Enforce tenant isolation using the current organization membership/context, and reject requests without a selected organization. Apply optional filters for department ID, employment type, and status, plus case-insensitive name search against the related member profile display name. Sort by a supported field, defaulting to created_at descending if no sort is provided. Return a paginated summary list with each row including employee identity, role, department, position title, employment type, status, and basic member/profile information needed for list views. Do not expose employees from other organizations. Validate that filter values are within the organization and that sort fields are allowed. If the caller lacks employee:view permission in the current organization, return a forbidden error.

responseBody.description: Paginated employee summaries for the active organization.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for the organization employee list.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single employee record within the current organization context.

This endpoint returns the employee's organization-scoped profile, including the linked user account, assigned role, optional department, position title, employment type, and current status. It is intended for employee detail pages and administrative review screens where the full employee record is required.

Access is limited by organization context and permissions. A user may view their own employee record, while users with employee view permission may view other employees in the same organization. The employee must belong to the selected organization; requests for employees outside the active context must be rejected. If the employee does not exist, or the caller is not authorized to view it, the request must fail with the appropriate not-found or forbidden response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the employee by primary key UUID and ensure the record belongs to the caller's selected organization. Reject access if the organization context is missing, the employee is not in that organization, or the caller lacks employee view permission and is not the owner of the employee record.

Return the employee with its referenced organization, member, role, and department relationships resolved as needed by the DTO. Do not expose records from other organizations. Use the schema fields exactly as defined: id, erp_hrm_time_organization_id, erp_hrm_time_member_id, erp_hrm_time_role_id, erp_hrm_time_department_id, position_title, employment_type, status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

Since this is a read-only detail endpoint, no mutation or locking is required. If the employee was deleted or is unavailable in the current organization context, return not found. If the caller cannot access the selected organization, return forbidden.

responseBody.description: Full employee record for the selected organization context.

parameters.description: Employee identifier in UUID format (organization-scoped via the selected organization context).
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Create a new employee record in the currently selected organization.

This endpoint is used by organization members with employee management permission to add a person to the organization, assign the employee’s role, and capture employment details such as department, position or title, and employment type. The employee record represents that user account’s participation in the selected organization and is always isolated to the current organization context.

The created employee must belong to exactly one organization and must be assigned exactly one role from that organization. The request must be rejected if the referenced role does not belong to the current organization, if the selected organization context is missing, or if the target user account is already represented as an employee in the same organization. Department assignment is optional, but when provided it must also belong to the same organization. The response returns the newly created employee record for immediate use in the UI.

Common validation failures include permission denial, invalid organization context, duplicate employee membership, and invalid references to role or department data. The operation should not expose or accept data outside the current organization scope.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Authorize the caller with employee management permission in the currently selected organization context.

Resolve the current organization from the auth/session context and reject the request if no organization is selected or the caller is not a member of that organization.

Validate the request body against the employee create contract. Ensure the referenced user account exists when the request links to an account, and prevent creation of more than one employee record for the same user account within the same organization. Verify that the role belongs to the current organization and that exactly one role is assigned. If a department is provided, verify that it belongs to the same organization. Validate the employment type against the supported set from the requirements: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern.

Persist the employee record within a transaction. If invitation-related behavior is implemented by the surrounding workflow, allow the service layer to connect a pending invitation or existing account association, but do not create cross-organization links. After insert, load the created employee with its organization-scoped relations needed by the API response.

Return standard authorization, validation, not-found, and conflict errors for missing permissions, invalid foreign keys, and duplicate employee membership. Do not allow any data from another organization to be attached or returned.

responseBody.description: The newly created employee record.

requestBody.description: Employee creation data for the current organization context.

operations.description:
Update an organization employee record.

This operation lets authorized organization staff modify an employee's record within the currently selected organization. It is used to maintain the employee's department assignment, position title, employment classification, role assignment, and current status as the organization changes over time.

The employee record is organization-scoped and links a member account to exactly one organization and one role, with an optional department. Changes must stay within the same organization context, and any department or role referenced must exist in that organization. If a department is removed from the organization, employee records are expected to clear that department reference rather than lose the employee record.

Validation errors should be returned when the employee does not exist in the selected organization, when a referenced department or role is invalid for the organization, or when a requested status change is not allowed by business rules. The API should also preserve the employee's historical timelogs, timesheets, and contracts while updating only the current employee record.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the employee by id within the selected organization context and reject the request if the record does not belong to that organization. Apply partial field updates only for fields present in the request body: erp_hrm_time_department_id, position_title, employment_type, erp_hrm_time_role_id, and status.

Validate that department changes reference an existing department in the same organization, or allow null to clear the assignment. Validate that role changes reference an existing role in the same organization and preserve the invariant that the employee has exactly one role. Validate employment_type against the allowed business values: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern. Validate status against the allowed employee states used by the system, and ensure deactivation/reactivation rules are enforced by the service layer.

Update updated_at automatically. Do not modify organization_id or member_id through this endpoint. Persist changes in a transaction and return the updated employee entity. If the employee is not found, return a not found error. If a referenced department or role is invalid for the organization, return a validation error. If the user lacks employee management permission, return a forbidden error.

responseBody.description: The updated employee record after the modification is applied.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the employee within the organization.
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: Fields that may be updated for an organization employee record.

A role must exist in the current organization before the employee can be assigned to it through erp_hrm_time_role_id.

operations.description:
Permanently removes an employee from the current organization.

This operation deletes the employee record identified by the path parameter from the selected organization context. It is intended for organization managers and other authorized users who can maintain employee records, and it must never affect employees in other organizations.

Before deletion, the service should verify that the target employee belongs to the active organization and that the caller has permission to manage employees in that organization. If the employee is referenced by other organization data, the deletion must honor database constraints and the organization rules defined for the platform. Historical data that is stored in other entities must be handled consistently by the persistence layer.

If the employee cannot be found in the current organization, or if the caller is not authorized to remove employee records, the request should fail with the appropriate validation or authorization error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the target employee by id within the current organization scope using the active organization context from the authenticated request.
Verify that the caller has employee management authority for the organization before attempting deletion.

Confirm the employee belongs to the active organization; return not found if the id exists in another organization or does not exist.
Delete the employee row directly through the employee repository. The employee schema defines organization, member, role, and optional department foreign keys with cascade relations, so rely on the database for referential cleanup and constraint enforcement.

Do not accept a request body. Do not perform partial updates or status changes here; this endpoint is a true deletion operation. If the database rejects the delete because of downstream references or policy constraints, propagate the error in a user-safe way.

parameters.description: Identifier of the employee to permanently delete within the current organization scope.
parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Retrieve the contract history for a specific employee.

This operation returns the employee’s historical employment contracts in chronological order so the caller can review how compensation and working terms changed over time. The history is the authoritative record for understanding when each employment period started, when it ended, and which contract is currently active.

The returned contracts belong to the employee identified in the path and are scoped to the current organization context. Past contracts remain unchanged as historical records, while the active contract may still be included as part of the sequence for review. This endpoint is intended for the employee’s own history and for authorized viewers with employee view permission within the organization.

Access is restricted by organization context and employee visibility rules. If the caller is not allowed to view the employee, the request must be rejected. If the employee does not exist in the current organization, the request must fail with a not-found error. For long histories, the response should support pagination and stable ordering.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the current organization context first and verify that the target employee belongs to that organization. Enforce authorization so that the caller may view their own contracts or must have employee:view permission to view another employee’s contracts.

Query erp_hrm_time_employee_contracts filtered by employee_id and the current organization scope. Sort results by start date ascending by default so the history reads in chronological order. Support pagination parameters and any reasonable sort override defined in the request DTO, but keep the default order stable for contract history browsing.

The request body must carry search and pagination controls only; do not include employeeId because it is already supplied in the path. Return a paginated summary collection using a contract summary type suitable for timeline rendering. Include the active contract and all historical contracts for the employee.

Handle these errors explicitly: employee not found in the selected organization, forbidden access when the caller lacks employee:view permission for another employee, and invalid pagination or sort inputs. No mutation occurs in this endpoint, and no historical contract data should be altered.

responseBody.description: Paginated employee contract history summaries.

parameters.description: The employee identifier whose contract history is being retrieved within the current organization context.
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: Search, sorting, and pagination criteria for the employee contract history.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single employee contract from an employee’s historical contract record.

This operation returns one stored employment contract for the requested employee, including the contract period, compensation terms, weekly working-time expectations, and optional notes. It is intended for reviewing how an employee’s employment terms changed over time and for inspecting the employee’s current active contract when needed.

Access is limited to the employee’s own contract history or to users who have permission to view employees within the organization. The contract must belong to the specified employee, and the employee must belong to the current organization context. The returned record is read-only and must be shown exactly as stored, preserving historical accuracy.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the employee by employeeId within the current organization context, then load the employee contract by employeeContractId constrained to that employee. Enforce that the contract row exists, belongs to the employee, and the employee belongs to the caller's current organization.

Authorize access for either the employee viewing their own contracts or a user with employee:view permission in the same organization. Reject cross-organization access. If the employee exists but the contract does not belong to them, return not found rather than exposing contract existence.

Return the full employee contract entity with id, employee reference, start/end dates, pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, notes, and timestamps. Do not include related collections. This is a read-only operation and must not alter active/previous contract logic.

responseBody.description: The requested employee contract record, returned as a read-only historical employment entry.

parameters.name: employeeId

operations.description:
Create a new employment contract for an employee.

This operation adds a historical contract record under the specified employee in the currently selected organization. It is used when an employee's compensation or working arrangement changes and a new contract period must begin while preserving previous contracts as part of the employee's employment history.

If the employee already has an active contract, the service closes that previous contract automatically by setting its end date to the day before the new contract starts. The new record becomes the current active contract for that employee, and past contracts remain unchanged as historical records.

Access is limited to users who are allowed to manage employees or otherwise view the employee's contract records. The employee identifier in the path defines the target scope, and the request body only contains the new contract terms. Errors should be returned when the employee does not exist in the current organization, when the caller lacks permission, when the start date is invalid, or when the new contract would overlap existing contract periods.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the employee within the current organization context, enforcing that the path employee belongs to the selected organization and is visible to the caller. Verify authorization: users with employee management access may create contracts, and users with employee view access may be allowed if business rules permit self-service or read-only contract context, but creation should generally require manage permission.

Validate the request body against the actual employee contract schema fields. Create the new contract with the provided start date, pay rate, pay period, working hours per week, and optional end date/notes. Ensure the start date and pay rate are present and that pay period is one of the supported enumerations. Reject negative or invalid numeric values and any contract payload that would violate historical ordering.

If the employee has an active contract, update that prior contract in the same transaction by setting its end date to the day before the new contract starts, unless the prior contract already ended. Prevent overlapping active periods and ensure only one active contract exists after completion. Preserve all past contracts without mutation except the automatic closure of the previous active contract.

Return the created contract entity after persistence. If the employee is missing, the organization context is invalid, the caller lacks authorization, or business validation fails, return the appropriate 4xx error. Use a transaction so that the prior contract update and the new contract insert are atomic.

responseBody.description: The newly created employee contract, including its effective terms and identifiers.

parameters.description: The employee identifier within the current organization.
parameters.name: employeeId

requestBody.description: The contract terms to create for the employee.

prerequisites.description: An employee record must exist in the current organization before a contract can be created for that employee.

operations.description:
Update an employee's active contract.

This operation lets authorized organization members change the current employment terms for a specific employee, including compensation, contract dates, working hours, and notes. The contract belongs to one employee and is part of that employee's historical employment record.

Only the active contract can be edited. Past contracts are immutable and must be rejected if they are no longer active. The update must preserve contract history, keep the employee scoped to the selected organization, and use the employee identifier in the path to ensure the contract belongs to the correct employee.

Requests may fail when the caller lacks employee management access, when the contract does not belong to the specified employee, when the contract is not the active contract, or when the updated values violate contract history rules such as overlapping active periods.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target employee contract by employeeContractId, verify it belongs to employeeId, and ensure both records are within the caller's selected organization context. Reject the request if the contract is not the employee's current active contract; past contracts must remain immutable.

Apply the incoming fields to the contract row using only the actual schema columns: start_date, end_date, pay_rate, pay_period, working_hours_per_week, and notes. Preserve created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, and the employee foreign key. Validate pay_period against the allowed contract values used by the business rules. Ensure start_date remains valid and does not create an invalid historical sequence. If the updated contract is the active one, keep it as the latest contract for that employee.

If the request changes the active contract's start date or other terms in a way that would conflict with historical continuity, reject the update. Do not update any contract that is no longer active. Return the updated contract entity after persistence. Emit appropriate not-found or forbidden errors when the employee-contract relationship is invalid or when the caller lacks permission.

responseBody.description: The updated employee contract record.

parameters.description: The employee identifier in the selected organization scope.
parameters.name: employeeId

parameters.description: The employee contract identifier within the employee's contract history.

operations.description:
Delete an employment contract record for a specific employee.

This operation removes the selected contract from the employee’s contract history within the current organization context. Employment contracts store compensation terms, working-time expectations, and the effective date range for an employee, so the contract being deleted must belong to the employee identified in the path.

The service must verify that the employee exists in the current organization, that the contract belongs to that employee, and that the caller has permission to manage employee records. Because contracts are historical business records, the implementation should apply the organization’s business rules for contract removal and reject attempts to remove a contract that is protected by current employment state or other invariants.

If the contract cannot be deleted because it does not exist, does not belong to the specified employee, or the caller lacks permission, the API should return the appropriate error response from the standard error handling layer. After successful deletion, the contract must no longer be returned by employee contract retrieval or contract history queries.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Resolve the employee within the active organization context, then resolve the contract by employee ID and contract ID.

Enforce that the contract belongs to the employee and that both records are inside the current organization scope. Use the contract table’s relationship to employee and honor the employee-scoped unique history model. Before deletion, apply business validation to ensure the record may be removed under the organization’s HR rules; if the contract is the current active contract or otherwise protected by business policy, reject the request with a conflict-style error.

If the implementation uses physical deletion, remove the row directly. If the service layer routes contract removal through the model’s deleted_at support, set the deleted marker consistently and exclude the record from normal queries. In either case, keep the employee record intact and do not cascade to other employee data.

Return no body on success. Ensure audit logging, if enabled by the application layer, records the deletion action with employee and contract identifiers.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of departments for the currently selected organization.

This operation is used to browse the organization’s internal department structure and support employee grouping. It returns department summary data that reflects the current organization scope, including the department name, description, and parent department relationship where applicable.

The list is available to employees for read-only visibility and to organization managers for administration. Results must never include departments from another organization, and the current organization context must be enforced on every request. When departments are deleted elsewhere, the visible list must reflect the current state of the organization’s hierarchy.

If the client requests search, filtering, or sorting combinations that cannot be satisfied, the service should return a validation error. Pagination must be applied consistently to avoid loading the entire organization department tree at once.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_departments within the currently selected organization only.
Apply organization scoping using erp_hrm_time_organization_id from the active member context.
Support search by department name and sorting over stable fields such as name and created_at, with pagination.
Respect the one-level hierarchy by returning parent department information, but do not recursively expand child departments.
Exclude departments belonging to other organizations and honor the current visible state of the table, including records that remain after deletions according to the business rules.
If the requester lacks organization context, reject the call as unauthorized/invalid context. If the request includes unsupported sort/filter values, return a validation error.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of department summaries for the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for organization department browsing.

operations.description:
Create a new department for the currently selected organization.

Departments are organizational groupings used to describe the internal structure of the company and help employees understand how staff are grouped. A department may include a short description and may optionally reference a single parent department, allowing only one level of hierarchy within the same organization.

This operation is restricted to users with organization management permission. The department name must be unique within the selected organization, and any parent department must belong to the same organization. If the request would create an invalid hierarchy or duplicate department structure, the system rejects it. When a department is created successfully, it becomes available in the organization’s department list for employees to view.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new erp_hrm_time_departments row for the currently selected organization.
Validate that the authenticated member has org:manage permission in the selected organization context.
Resolve the optional parent department within the same organization; reject the request if the parent does not exist, belongs to another organization, or would create deeper nesting than one level.
Enforce the unique constraint on (erp_hrm_time_organization_id, name) and return a conflict-style validation error if a duplicate name exists in the organization.
Persist name, optional description, optional parent_department_id, organization id from context, and timestamps. Do not accept organization id from the request body.
If the database schema or business validation detects duplicate or confusing department structure, surface a domain validation error rather than creating the record.
Return the created department entity with its identifiers and descriptive fields.

responseBody.description: The newly created department record.

requestBody.description: Department creation data for the selected organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a department within the selected organization.

Departments are organizational groupings used to describe the internal structure of an organization and to support staff grouping. This operation returns the department’s identity, name, optional description, optional parent department, and audit timestamps so clients can display the current organizational structure.

The result is limited to the currently selected organization. If the department does not belong to the active organization context, or if the caller is not allowed to view department data in that organization, the request must be rejected. The department hierarchy is shallow and only supports a single parent department, so the returned data must not imply deeper nesting than the schema allows.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the department by primary key and verify that its organization matches the caller’s selected organization context before returning it. Use a single-row lookup on erp_hrm_time_departments.id, and include the parent department reference if present.

If the record is missing or belongs to another organization, return a not-found or forbidden-style error according to the service’s standard authorization model. Do not expose departments across organization boundaries. Do not require management permission for read access if the business rules allow employees to view department lists and details.

Return the full department entity DTO mapped from the schema fields only: id, erp_hrm_time_organization_id, parent_department_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at if the API contract includes it. Preserve the optional parent reference but do not expand recursive children to avoid circular payloads.

responseBody.description: Full department details for the selected organization.
