operations.description:
Update a department within the current organization.

This operation edits the department name, description, and optional parent department used to organize employees and describe the organization structure. Departments are organization-scoped, and the updated department must remain within the selected organization context.

The parent department relationship is limited to one level of nesting. The service must validate that the requested parent department, when provided, belongs to the same organization, is not the department itself, and does not create a deeper hierarchy or a duplicate/confusing department structure. Department names must remain unique within the organization.

If the department cannot be found in the selected organization, if the target parent is invalid, or if the change would violate department structure rules, the request must be rejected with an appropriate validation error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the department by id and current organization scope. Reject the request if the department does not belong to the selected organization or is unavailable. Validate that the new name is unique within the same organization, excluding the current department record.

If parentDepartmentId is provided, confirm that the parent exists, belongs to the same organization, and is not equal to the current department id. Enforce the single-level hierarchy rule by preventing any change that would create deeper nesting or an invalid parent-child structure. Also reject updates that would create a duplicate or confusing department structure within the organization.

Update only editable fields: name, description, and parentDepartmentId. Do not modify organization ownership, created_at, updated_at directly, or any employee assignments. Return the updated department record after persistence.

responseBody.description: The updated department record.

parameters.description: Department identifier in the selected organization (UUID).
parameters.name: departmentId

requestBody.description: Editable department fields for the current organization.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a department from the current organization.

This operation removes an organization-scoped department record used to group employees and describe the internal structure of the organization. The department may have an optional parent department, but the hierarchy remains limited to a single nesting level.

When the department is deleted, any employees assigned to it must keep their employee records and have their department cleared. If the department is used as a parent department, that relationship is removed as part of deleting the department itself. All checks must be performed within the selected organization context so departments from other organizations cannot be affected.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the department by id and the current organization context, and verify that it belongs to the selected organization.
If the department does not exist or is outside the organization context, return a not-found or forbidden-style error according to the service conventions.
Before deletion, identify employees whose erp_hrm_time_department_id matches the department id and clear that foreign key so employee records are preserved.
Then delete the department record. Because the schema defines recursive parent/child department relations, deleting the department must also remove the parent-child association for that record; cascading behavior should not be relied on without confirming the service layer explicitly nullifies or reassigns affected employees.
Ensure the operation is transactional so employee updates and department deletion succeed or fail together.
Do not allow deletion to cross organization boundaries. Emit the appropriate organization activity log entry if the application records destructive department actions.

parameters.description: Department identifier within the current organization.
parameters.name: departmentId

operations.description:
Retrieve the direct child departments for a department.

This endpoint returns the departments that are nested immediately under the specified parent department within the currently selected organization. It supports viewing the organization structure used for staff grouping and internal organization planning, while keeping the hierarchy limited to a single parent level.

The result is read-only and scoped to the active organization context. If the department does not belong to the selected organization, or if the requested parent cannot be resolved, the request must be rejected. Child departments are returned as summaries suitable for list views, including the department name and description used to identify the grouping.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the parent department by id and verify it belongs to the currently selected organization. Query erp_hrm_time_departments for records where parent_department_id equals the parent id, erp_hrm_time_organization_id matches the current organization, and deleted_at is null if the service filters retained rows.

Apply pagination, search, and sorting from the request body. Search should target department name and optionally description if supported by the list DTO. The operation must only expose direct children and must not traverse deeper descendants, because the business rule limits department nesting to one level.

Return a paginated summary list. If the parent department is outside the selected organization, respond with a not-found or forbidden-style domain error according to the service convention. Do not include employee assignments in this response; this endpoint only exposes department structure.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of direct child department summaries for the selected parent department.

parameters.description: The parent department identifier within the currently selected organization.
parameters.name: departmentId

requestBody.description: Pagination, search, and sorting criteria for retrieving child departments.

operations.description:
Retrieve a child department that belongs under a specific parent department within the current organization.

This endpoint is used to inspect a department in the organization structure when the caller already knows the parent department context. It returns the department’s identity, organization scope, parent reference, name, description, and timestamps from the department record.

The child department must be directly associated with the supplied parent department and must belong to the currently selected organization. If the parent-child relationship does not match, or if either record is outside the active organization, the request must be rejected. The operation is read-only and is available for department browsing in accordance with the organization’s internal structure rules.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the child department by matching id = childDepartmentId and erp_hrm_time_organization_id to the current organization context, while also verifying parent_department_id = departmentId. Return the full department record if found.

Enforce organization isolation on both identifiers. If the parent department does not exist in the selected organization, or the child department is not directly nested under that parent, return a not-found or forbidden-style domain error consistent with the service error contract.

Do not infer any hidden hierarchy fields beyond the actual schema. Use the department table only, selecting id, erp_hrm_time_organization_id, parent_department_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at. Respect the one-level hierarchy constraint already defined by the domain rules. No request body is required.

responseBody.description: The requested child department within the parent department scope.

parameters.description: The parent department identifier within the current organization scope.
parameters.name: departmentId

parameters.description: The child department identifier within the current organization scope.
parameters.name: childDepartmentId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of roles for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint returns the organization’s access-role definitions, including the built-in Owner, Manager, and Employee roles and any custom roles created within that organization. It is intended for role management screens where users need to browse, search, and filter role definitions in the active organization context.

The result set is always scoped to the selected organization and must not include roles from any other tenant. Consumers can use the list to inspect role names and permission sets, and to support workflows for assigning employees or maintaining custom role definitions.

If the current organization context is missing or invalid, or if the caller lacks permission to view roles in the selected organization, the request should fail with an authorization or context error. The service must preserve the built-in role set and return them alongside any organization-created custom roles according to the applied filters and sorting rules.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query erp_hrm_time_roles within the selected organization context only.
Apply organization scoping from the authenticated member’s active organization selection before any search/filter logic.

Support request-body search criteria for pagination, free-text search by role name, sorting, and any additional filters supported by the role request DTO. The query should return built-in roles and custom roles that belong to the same organization. Built-in roles are permanent and must always remain visible in the organization scope.

Return a paginated summary projection rather than full role records. The summary should be optimized for list browsing and should include role identity, name, and permission composition information if the summary schema exposes it. Do not cross organizations or infer roles from other tenants.

If the organization context is absent, reject the request as unauthorized or invalid-context. If the caller does not have permission to view roles in the selected organization, reject with a forbidden error. Validate pagination bounds and search inputs according to the request DTO. Handle empty results with a valid empty page response.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of role summaries for the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, sort, and pagination criteria for browsing roles in the selected organization.

operations.description:
Create a new role in the currently selected organization.

This operation lets an organization owner define a custom role with a name, an optional description, and a validated set of permissions. Roles are organization-scoped records, so the created role belongs only to the active organization and does not affect other tenants. Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee are part of the organization role model but are not created through this endpoint.

The role name must be unique within the organization. The permission set must be composed only from approved platform permissions, and the implementation must persist the role together with its role-permission links in a single consistent workflow. If the organization context is missing or the caller lacks role-management access, the request must be rejected. If the requested role name already exists in the organization, the request must fail with a validation conflict.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Validate that the caller has organization-level role management access in the currently selected organization. Resolve the active organization context before any write.

Check that the request body contains a role name and only approved permissions. Enforce uniqueness of role name within the organization using the existing `(organization_id, name)` constraint. Reject attempts to create built-in roles through this endpoint; built-in roles are system-defined records that already exist for each organization.

Insert the role record first, then insert the role-permission bridge rows for each validated permission in the same transaction. If any permission key is unknown, reject the entire request. Return the created role with its assigned permissions after persistence. Ensure the operation emits any required audit/activity record according to the organization role-management rules.

responseBody.description: The newly created organization role with its assigned permissions.

requestBody.description: Role creation payload for the active organization. Includes the role name, optional description, and the approved permissions that compose the role.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single role within the currently selected organization.

This endpoint returns the role record identified by its ID, including the role name, description, and whether it is a built-in role. Roles are organization-scoped, so the result always belongs to the active organization context and must not expose roles from other organizations.

Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee are returned through the same endpoint as custom roles. Consumers should use the `isBuiltin` flag and the role name to distinguish protected system roles from organization-created roles. If the role does not exist in the current organization context, the server must return a not-found response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the role by primary key and verify it belongs to the currently selected organization context before returning it. Use the authenticated member's organization scope to prevent cross-tenant access.

Query the `erp_hrm_time_roles` table by `id`, and ensure the matched row's `erp_hrm_time_organization_id` equals the active organization. Exclude deleted rows if the application treats `deleted_at` as unavailable data for consumers.

Return the role entity fields defined in the schema: `id`, `erp_hrm_time_organization_id`, `name`, `description`, `is_builtin`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, and `deleted_at` if the API contract exposes it. If the role is not found or does not belong to the active organization, respond with 404. Do not include permission assignments here unless a separate schema-backed relationship endpoint exists.

responseBody.description: The role record for the requested ID within the current organization context.

parameters.description: Role identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: roleId

operations.description:
Update an organization role definition.

This operation lets an organization owner or other authorized member update a role that belongs to the currently selected organization. Roles define how access and responsibility are organized within the tenant, and the updated role remains scoped to that organization only. Built-in roles are always present in every organization and must remain unchanged by this operation.

Custom roles may be renamed and their permission set may be adjusted using approved organization permissions. The service must validate that the role exists in the current organization, reject attempts to modify built-in roles, and ensure that every requested permission is valid for the organization role model. If the role is currently assigned to employees, the update must preserve those assignments while applying the new role definition.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target role by roleId within the active organization context. Verify that the role belongs to the organization associated with the request and that the caller has the required authorization, typically owner-managed role administration or equivalent permissions.

Disallow updates to built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee). If the role is built-in, return a domain validation error. For custom roles, apply the incoming name and permission changes in a single transaction. Validate the submitted permission list against the approved permission catalog and reject unknown or disallowed permissions.

Because roles are organization-scoped, never allow cross-organization updates. If the role does not exist in the current organization, return not found. After a successful update, return the updated role entity with its organization reference and current permission set. Keep employee-role assignments intact; do not cascade reassignment or unlink employees during a role update. If the role name would conflict with another role in the same organization, reject the request with a uniqueness error.

responseBody.description: The updated organization role after the changes have been applied.

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the role to update within the current organization context.
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: Role update data containing the new role name and permission set.

operations.description:
Permanently remove an organization role.

This operation deletes a role that belongs to the currently selected organization. It is intended for organization owners managing custom access structures. Built-in roles remain protected and cannot be removed.

The system rejects deletion when the target role is still assigned to one or more employees, because every employee in an organization must always keep exactly one role. Clients should expect errors when attempting to delete a built-in role, a role outside the active organization context, or a custom role that is still in use.

When the deletion succeeds, the role record is removed from the organization and any access configuration depending on that role should be refreshed by the caller.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Load the role by id within the authenticated member's selected organization context. Verify the role belongs to that organization before any destructive action. Reject the request if the role is marked as built-in, because built-in roles are permanently protected. Reject the request if any employee references the role, since each employee must retain exactly one role. If validation passes, delete the role record inside a transaction and rely on database cascade behavior only for dependent role-permission rows if the schema supports it; do not delete or modify employees. Return a not-found error when the id does not resolve within the organization context. Return a conflict or validation error when the role is in use or protected. Record any required activity audit entry if the service layer uses organization activity tracking for role changes.

parameters.description: Role identifier within the organization (global UUID primary key).
parameters.name: roleId

operations.description:
Search and browse the approved permission catalog.

This operation returns the canonical list of permissions recognized by the platform for composing organization role permission sets. Each permission entry includes a stable key and a human-readable description so role editors can choose only valid permissions when creating or updating custom roles.

The catalog is read-only from the API consumer perspective and reflects the records stored in `erp_hrm_time_permissions`. Results can be filtered, sorted, and paginated for admin-style browsing. Consumers should use this endpoint when they need to display or validate the available permission set before assigning permissions to roles.

If the caller is not authorized to inspect permission metadata, the request must be rejected. Invalid search filters or unsupported sort fields should also be rejected with a clear validation error.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the erp_hrm_time_permissions table as the authoritative permission catalog.
Apply optional search against key and description, support pagination and sorting, and exclude deleted records unless the service contract explicitly requires showing retired permissions.
Return a paginated summary projection containing the permission identity, key, and description fields only; do not expose internal audit columns in the summary list.
Enforce access control at the service layer before querying, because permission metadata should only be visible to authorized organization administrators or privileged members.
Validate request filter values and sort fields against the allowed list. Reject unknown filters, invalid sort directions, and out-of-range pagination values.
Use a stable deterministic order when no sort is provided, such as key ascending.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of permission catalog entries.

requestBody.description: Search, filter, pagination, and sorting criteria for browsing the permission catalog.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single approved permission from the canonical permission catalog.

This operation returns the stable permission identifier, the permission key used by the authorization layer, and the human-readable description that explains what the permission allows. It is intended for role-management and administrative screens that need to inspect the platform’s approved permission vocabulary before assigning permissions to organization roles.

The permission catalog is shared across the platform and is the source of truth for valid role permissions. Consumers should use this endpoint when they need to display or verify an individual permission entry by its identifier. If the permission does not exist, the service should return a not-found response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Resolve the permission by its UUID primary key from erp_hrm_time_permissions.
Return the record only if it exists and is not deleted. Do not infer or synthesize permissions from the key list; read the row directly. Because the catalog is global and not organization-scoped, no organization context filter is applied.

Implementation should use a single indexed lookup on id, with a not-found error when no record matches. Keep the response read-only. If the deleted_at column is populated, treat the row as inactive and do not return it unless the broader codebase explicitly exposes retired permissions, which is not indicated here. Ensure the endpoint is protected so only appropriately authorized administrative users can access it, consistent with role management flows.

responseBody.description: A single approved permission from the catalog.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the permission record (UUID).
parameters.name: permissionId

operations.description:
Update the permission set assigned to an organization role.

This operation allows organization owners and other authorized members to change which approved permissions are attached to a role within the currently selected organization. The role is evaluated in the context of its parent organization, and the change applies only within that tenant boundary.

Only permissions from the organization’s approved catalog may be assigned. Built-in roles such as Owner, Manager, and Employee keep their predefined business meaning and must be protected from invalid permission changes according to the organization rules and permission model. If the requested permission list contains unsupported values, the request must be rejected with a validation error.

The updated role is returned after persistence so consumers can immediately refresh authorization-dependent screens and caches. If the role does not exist in the current organization, or the caller lacks organization management access, the request must fail with an appropriate authorization or not-found response.
operations.name: updatePermissions
operations.specification:
Load the role by roleId within the current organization context. Verify the caller has organization management permission or equivalent owner access. Reject the request if the role does not belong to the active organization.

Validate the submitted permission list against the approved organization permission catalog. Ensure every permission is unique and belongs to the allowed set. If the role is a built-in role, enforce the business rules that prevent unauthorized customization of its fixed permission model; if the platform allows any limited update for built-ins, apply those constraints here, otherwise reject the update.

Persist the updated permission assignment in the role-permission relation table in a transaction. Remove previous permission mappings for that role and insert the new approved mappings atomically so the role never ends up in a partially updated state. Return the refreshed role representation after update. On validation failure, return a clear error indicating whether the issue is an invalid permission or an unauthorized role mutation. On not found, return a role-scoped 404. On forbidden access, return 403.

responseBody.description: The role after its permission set has been updated.

parameters.description: Identifier of the role to update within the current organization context.
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: The new approved permission set to assign to the role.

operations.description:
Assign one or more approved permissions to an organization role.

This operation adds permission entries to the selected role so the role can represent the correct access responsibility within the organization. It is intended for custom role administration and uses the role's organization scope to ensure permission changes stay within the same tenant.

The role must belong to the currently selected organization, and the permission set must come from the approved permission catalog. Built-in roles are protected by business rules and must not be modified through this endpoint. If a requested permission is already assigned, the operation should ignore the duplicate or reject it according to service policy, but it must not create duplicate role-permission rows.

Permission assignment errors should be reported clearly when the role does not exist, belongs to another organization, is not editable, or when any requested permission key is outside the approved list.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target role by id and verify it belongs to the active organization context. Reject the request if the role is missing, deleted, or not organization-scoped to the current tenant.

Validate that the role is editable: built-in roles must not be modified. If the role is protected, return a forbidden or conflict-level domain error according to the service convention.

Resolve each requested permission key against erp_hrm_time_permissions.key. Only approved catalog entries are allowed. Reject unknown keys before inserting any join rows.

Insert rows into erp_hrm_time_role_permissions for each requested permission that is not already linked to the role. Use a transaction so the permission set is applied atomically. If duplicates are provided in the request, de-duplicate them in memory before insertion.

Return the updated role representation including its assigned permissions. Preserve existing role metadata. Do not modify the role record itself; only create missing role-permission associations.

responseBody.description: The updated role with its current permission assignments after the new permissions have been added.

parameters.description: The role identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: roleId

requestBody.description: Permission keys to assign to the selected role. Each key must exist in the approved permission catalog.

operations.description:
Retrieve a permission assignment for a specific role within the selected organization.

This endpoint returns one role-permission link record, including the permission granted to the role and the timestamps for the association. It is intended for role management screens where an organization owner or other authorized member needs to inspect the exact permission set attached to a role.

The role is organization-scoped, so the role identifier and the role-permission identifier must belong to the same organization context. The system should verify that the permission assignment exists for the requested role before returning it. If the role or permission assignment does not exist, or if the permission assignment is not attached to the specified role, the request must fail with a not-found error.

Access to this endpoint follows organization role permissions. Built-in roles and custom roles are both viewable when the caller has access to role management or role inspection functionality within the selected organization.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the role-permission row by its UUID primary key and verify that erp_hrm_time_role_id matches the supplied roleId path parameter. Join the related erp_hrm_time_permissions row so the response can include the assigned permission details.

Enforce organization context by resolving the role through the current selected organization and rejecting cross-organization access. If the role-permission record does not exist, is soft-deleted, or does not belong to the requested role, return not found.

Because this is a read-only detail endpoint, do not mutate any data. Include the related permission object in the response and keep the shape stable for UI inspection of role permission sets.

responseBody.description: The role-permission assignment with its linked permission details.

parameters.description: Role identifier in UUID format within the selected organization.
parameters.name: roleId

parameters.description: Role-permission assignment identifier in UUID format.
parameters.name: rolePermissionId

prerequisites.description: A role-permission assignment must be created for the specified role before it can be retrieved by rolePermissionId.

operations.description:
Remove a permission from an organization role.

This operation deletes a single role-permission assignment from the role's approved permission set. It is used to adjust a custom role's access scope within the selected organization and to keep the role's permission list aligned with the organization's approved permission catalog.

The role must belong to the current organization context, and the permission assignment must belong to that role. Built-in roles remain protected by application rules, so attempts to remove permissions from a protected built-in role should be rejected when the broader business rules require it. If the specified assignment does not exist, the request must fail with a not-found error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the target role by roleId within the current organization context, then load the role-permission assignment by rolePermissionId constrained to that role.
Verify that the assignment exists and belongs to the role; otherwise return a not-found error.
Apply business-rule validation before deletion: do not allow deletion when the role is protected by system rules that forbid modification, and preserve organization scoping so one organization cannot affect another organization's role data.
Delete the role-permission row from erp_hrm_time_role_permissions using the junction row id. Because the schema includes a deleted_at column, follow the service's established deletion behavior for this entity: if the application uses physical deletion for this endpoint, remove the row; if it uses repository-level deletion semantics, ensure the row is no longer returned in active permission queries.
Do not return a body. If the role or assignment is missing, or the role is outside the selected organization context, respond with the appropriate not-found or forbidden error.

parameters.description: The role identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: roleId

parameters.description: The role-permission assignment identifier scoped to the specified role.
parameters.name: rolePermissionId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of projects for the currently selected organization.

This operation is used by project browsers and dashboards to show projects that belong to the active organization context. Results can be filtered by status and searched by project name or description, while keeping all data isolated to the selected organization.

Each returned project summary includes the fields needed for list rendering, including the project name, color code for visual distinction, lifecycle status, and basic schedule metadata. Access is limited to users with project view permission in the current organization, and the response must never include projects from any other organization.

If the requester lacks the required permission, the service must reject the call. When filters are applied, the query must remain constrained to the active organization and must honor pagination and sorting rules consistently.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Build an organization-scoped project search query against erp_hrm_time_projects.
Enforce project:view permission before executing the query.
Resolve the active organization from the authenticated member's selected organization context and filter by erp_hrm_time_organization_id only; never accept organization scope from the request body.

Support pagination, search, and sorting in the request DTO. Search should match project name and description using the available text indexes. Support status filtering within the current organization only. Sort results deterministically, with a stable secondary ordering such as created_at or id when needed.

Return a paginated collection of project summaries. Summaries should include the project id, name, description, color code, status, budget hours, start date, end date, created_at, and updated_at fields as appropriate for the summary schema. Do not expose deleted records if the application treats deleted_at as non-listable.

Validate that the selected organization context exists and that the user has access to it. Reject unauthorized access, missing organization context, and malformed pagination or filter payloads with standard validation or authorization errors. Ensure the query never leaks projects from other organizations even when names or statuses overlap.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project summaries for the current organization.

requestBody.description: Project search, pagination, filtering, and sorting criteria for the current organization.

operations.description:
Create a new project in the currently selected organization.

This operation is used by users who have project management permission to register a project record that can later be assigned employees, tasks, and time entries. A project belongs to exactly one organization and is identified within that organization by its name and lifecycle metadata. The project record stores the human-readable name, optional description, required display color code, status, estimated budget hours, and optional start and end dates.

Project names must be unique within the organization. The project color code is required so the project can be visually distinguished in lists and planning views. The status determines whether the project is active, archived, or completed, and created projects should follow the business rules for valid status initialization. If the organization context is missing or the caller lacks project management permission, the request must be rejected. Validation errors should be returned when required fields are missing, the color code is invalid, the status is not allowed, or the project would violate organization-scoped uniqueness.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Insert a new row into erp_hrm_time_projects using the current organization context as erp_hrm_time_organization_id.

Authorize the caller with project management permission in the selected organization. Validate that name is present, colorCode is present, and status is one of active, archived, or completed. Validate optional budgetHours, startDate, and endDate if provided. Enforce the unique constraint on (erp_hrm_time_organization_id, name) and map conflicts to a domain validation error.

Set createdAt and updatedAt from the persistence layer. Do not accept id, organization id, createdAt, updatedAt, or deletedAt from the client. Persist description as nullable text. If the business layer enforces status defaults, apply the project creation default there rather than in the API contract. Return the created project as a full entity response.

responseBody.description: The newly created project record.

requestBody.description: Project details to create within the selected organization.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single project for the currently selected organization.

This operation returns the full project record, including the project name, optional description, required display color, lifecycle status, budgeted hours, and optional schedule dates. Projects belong to a single organization, and the returned record is always restricted to the caller's active organization context.

Access is limited to members who have project viewing permission in the current organization. If the project does not exist in the selected organization, or if the caller lacks permission, the request must be rejected. The response is intended for project detail screens and for workflows that need the full project object before editing, assigning members, or reviewing related tasks and time entries.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the project by its UUID primary key and ensure it belongs to the caller's selected organization.
Join is not required because all fields needed for the project entity are stored on erp_hrm_time_projects.
Enforce authorization for project viewing before returning data.
Return a not-found error when the id does not match a project in the active organization.
Do not expose projects from other organizations under any circumstance.
Exclude deleted records if the implementation treats deleted_at as inactive, but only if the project service already uses that column for filtering.
Return the full project entity with organization-scoped identifiers and lifecycle metadata.

responseBody.description: The full project record for the selected organization.

parameters.description: The project identifier (UUID primary key) within the selected organization.
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Update an existing project in the currently selected organization.

This operation lets authorized users modify a project’s core identity, planning data, lifecycle state, and display metadata. Projects are organization-scoped records that store the project name, optional description, required color code, status, budget hours, and optional start and end dates. The project name must remain unique within the organization.

The project remains linked to its existing organization, memberships, tasks, and timelog history after the update. Status changes must respect project lifecycle rules, including archived and completed states remaining available for viewing while preventing new timelogs from being added once the project is no longer active.

The service must reject requests that violate organization scope, uniqueness, or business validation rules. Typical errors include missing project access, duplicate project name within the organization, invalid status values, and invalid date or budget data.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target project by id and verify it belongs to the currently selected organization. Enforce project management permission before allowing updates.

Update only the project fields defined in the schema: name, description, color_code, status, budget_hours, start_date, and end_date. Do not change organization ownership or any relational data such as memberships, tasks, or timelogs.

Validate that name remains unique within erp_hrm_time_organization_id using the existing unique constraint. Validate color_code as a required UI display value, and ensure status is one of the allowed lifecycle states. Preserve existing archived/completed projects for viewing; status changes should not affect historical linked timelogs.

When updating dates, enforce sane chronology if the business layer requires it, and reject invalid budget hours or malformed values. Return the updated project record after persistence. If the project does not exist in the current organization, return not found. If permission is missing, return forbidden.

responseBody.description: The updated project record.

parameters.description: Identifier of the project to update.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Project fields to update.

operations.description:
Permanently deletes a project from the current organization context.

This operation is intended for project managers who need to remove a project that is no longer required. The project must belong to the active organization, and the caller must have permission to manage projects in that organization.

A project cannot be deleted when it still has timelogs associated with it. This protects recorded work history and ensures that time-tracking data remains available for reporting and audit purposes. If the project is already linked to any timelog, the request must be rejected.

On success, the project record is removed and the client should refresh any project lists or project-specific views. If the project does not exist, belongs to another organization, or the caller lacks access, the request must fail with the appropriate authorization or not-found error.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the project by projectId within the current organization context.
Verify the caller has project management permission for the active organization.
If the project does not exist in the current organization, return not found.
Before deletion, check whether any timelogs reference the project. If at least one timelog exists, reject the delete request and do not modify data.
If no timelogs are associated, delete the project record in a transaction. Ensure related project membership and task records are handled according to database constraints and surrounding service rules; do not remove timelogs because the business rule forbids deleting a project with existing timelog history.
Return no body on success. Emit any required activity/audit event after successful deletion if the system records project lifecycle actions.

parameters.description: The identifier of the project to delete within the current organization context.
parameters.name: projectId

operations.description:
Retrieve the paginated list of employees assigned to a project.

This endpoint returns the current project team composition for the specified project, including each membership's employee assignment and project role. It is used to display who participates in the project and whether a person is a regular member or a project lead.

The result is scoped to the current organization and to the selected project only. If the caller does not have permission to view the project, if the project does not belong to the active organization, or if the project cannot be found, the request must fail with the appropriate authorization or not-found response.

Because the project team is built from project memberships, the list always reflects the live staffing state. The response is paginated so large teams can be browsed efficiently, and the search criteria may include paging, sorting, and other list filters supported by the service contract.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Resolve the target project by projectId within the current organization context.
Verify the caller has access to view the project team; reuse project:view or project:manage authorization rules as defined by the service layer.

Query erp_hrm_time_project_memberships filtered by the target project and join the related employee record for display-friendly summary data. Preserve organization isolation by ensuring the project belongs to the current organization before querying memberships.

Support pagination, search, and sorting in the request body. Return memberships ordered according to the requested sort, with a stable default order for deterministic paging. The list should expose the membership role and the employee identity needed for the project team view, but should not leak memberships from other projects or organizations.

If the project does not exist in the active organization, return not found. If the caller lacks permission, return forbidden. If pagination parameters are invalid, return validation errors consistent with the API conventions.

responseBody.description: Paginated project membership summaries for the selected project.

parameters.description: The identifier of the project whose memberships will be listed.
parameters.name: projectId

requestBody.description: Pagination, search, and sorting criteria for the project membership list.

operations.description:
Create a project membership for an employee within the selected project.

This operation assigns one employee to one project and records the employee's role in that project, such as member or project lead. The project membership becomes the source of truth for who participates on the project team and in what capacity.

The project is identified by the path parameter, and the request body supplies the employee to assign along with the project-specific role. The system must reject duplicate assignments for the same project and employee combination, and it must verify that both the project and employee exist in the current organization context before creating the membership.

If the employee is already assigned to the project, the request must fail instead of creating a duplicate record. If either the project or employee is not accessible in the current organization scope, the request must be rejected with an authorization or not-found style error depending on the service's existing conventions.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target project by projectId within the current organization context and verify the caller has project management permission.
Validate that the employee exists in the same organization and is eligible to be assigned to the project.
Enforce the unique constraint on (erp_hrm_time_project_id, erp_hrm_time_employee_id); if a membership already exists, return a conflict-style error and do not insert a duplicate row.

The response supports list-oriented consumption and should surface fields that help the UI show the recorded date, duration, project context, task context, and billable state. Timelogs that belong to approved timesheets must remain visible but are locked against modification in their detail and mutation operations.

Requests that target another organization or violate visibility rules must be rejected. Requests that attempt to query outside the caller's current organization context or beyond the caller's permission scope should return an authorization or context error. Invalid pagination, sorting, or filter values should be rejected with validation errors.

Query erp_hrm_time_timelogs within the active organization context.

The system also rejects creation when the project is archived or completed, or when the employee is deactivated.

Errors are returned for invalid dates, missing required fields, project/task mismatches, unauthorized access, and business-rule violations such as trying to log time against a closed project. The timer resource is organization-scoped and must be evaluated against the authenticated member's current organization context. The service must ensure that the caller only receives timers that belong to employees in the selected organization and that any running timer shown to a member is the one associated with their own employee record.

If the request includes search or filtering criteria, the service should apply them within the selected organization and preserve the rule that each employee can have at most one active timer. Invalid access, missing organization context, or attempts to read timer data outside the current organization should be rejected.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Implement a PATCH collection endpoint for timers that reads from erp_hrm_time_timers under the authenticated member's selected organization context.

Resolve the current organization from the member session/context and reject the request if no organization is selected. Restrict visibility to timers owned by employees in that organization. If the caller is an employee, default the result set to their own timer records unless the request explicitly targets organization-wide browsing and the caller has sufficient permissions.

Support pagination, search, and sorting in the request body because this is a collection endpoint. Common filters should include active/running state, employee ownership, project, and date/time boundaries if present in the request contract. When returning a running timer, include the associated project and task references only if they belong to the same organization and are valid for the employee.

Enforce the business rule that only one active timer may exist per employee. If the implementation exposes the current timer for the logged-in employee, return at most one active record. Do not allow inactive/discarded/stopped timer records to be modified here; this endpoint is read-only.

Handle authorization strictly: members need organization context, and any organization-wide timer browsing must require the appropriate time-view permission. Return not found or forbidden responses when the timer or organization scope cannot be resolved. Ensure the response shape uses the timer summary or page type expected by the list/search contract.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timer summaries for the current organization context.

requestBody.description: Timer search, pagination, and sorting criteria for the selected organization context.

operations.description:
Start a new live timer for the current employee.

This operation creates the running timer record that captures an employee’s active work session within the selected organization. The timer stores the chosen project, an optional task, and an optional free-text description so the live session can be tracked with the correct context while work is in progress.

A user can have only one active timer at a time for the employee record associated with the authenticated account. The server must reject requests when a timer already exists for that employee, when the selected project is outside the current organization, or when an optional task does not belong to the selected project. The created timer becomes the source for later stop or discard actions, and stopping it will generate a timelog from the elapsed duration.

This endpoint is scoped to the current organization and employee context. If the employee is deactivated, the request must be rejected. If project or task relationships are invalid, the server must return a validation error rather than creating an inconsistent live session.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member’s current organization and employee record before creating the timer. Verify the employee belongs to the selected organization and is active. Enforce the one-active-timer rule by checking the unique employee_id constraint / existing timer row for the employee.

Validate that project_id belongs to the current organization. If task_id is provided, validate that the task belongs to the same project and organization. Persist member_id, employee_id, project_id, task_id, started_at, and optional description. started_at should be set by the server to the current time; do not accept it from the client.

Return the newly created timer record. Ensure the implementation runs in a transaction if any additional lookup or guard is needed, and surface a conflict error when an active timer already exists for the employee. Do not allow creation for deactivated employees or cross-organization project/task references.

responseBody.description: The newly created running timer for the current employee.

requestBody.description: Timer start details including the selected project, optional task, and optional running description.

operations.description:
Retrieve the currently running timer for the selected organization and authenticated employee.

This operation returns the live timer session record, including the selected project, optional task, start timestamp, and description. The timer represents an active work session that continues until it is stopped or discarded, and the response is intended for the employee’s running-timer view and related time-tracking UI.

The timer is organization-scoped and belongs to a specific employee, member account, project, and optionally a task. Consumers should use this operation to display the active session state and confirm which project and task are being tracked. If no timer exists for the requested identifier, or if the timer does not belong to the current organization context, the request must be rejected.

Because this endpoint exposes live time-tracking data, the implementation must enforce organization context and employee ownership rules. Access should be limited to the authenticated member associated with the timer unless broader administrative access is explicitly granted by the authorization layer.
operations.name: getByTimerid
operations.specification:
Load the timer by primary key and join its related member, employee, project, and optional task records so the full live-session context can be returned.
Verify that the timer belongs to the authenticated user's current organization context through the linked employee and organization membership. Reject access if the timer is not scoped to the current organization or if the caller is not authorized to view it.

Return the full timer entity using the timer DTO, preserving the live fields startedAt and description together with the selected project and optional task references. Do not mutate any state in this operation.

Handle not-found and authorization failures explicitly. If the timer has been discarded or otherwise no longer exists in the active dataset, return a not-found response.

responseBody.description: The running timer record with its live work-session context.

parameters.description: The timer identifier in UUID form.
parameters.name: timerId

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of timesheets for the currently selected organization.

This endpoint supports browsing timesheets by status and date range so employees can find their own weekly submissions and approvers can review submitted work. Results are always limited to the active organization context, and the returned rows must never include timesheets from any other organization.

Employees may only see their own timesheets unless they have approval permissions that allow broader access. Users with approval permission can review all submitted timesheets in the organization, while regular employees remain restricted to their own records. The list is designed for weekly time reporting workflows and should include summary data suitable for table views.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Read timesheets from erp_hrm_time_timesheets using the current organization context derived from authentication/session state. Join or filter through organization-linked employee records so that only timesheets belonging to the selected organization are returned.

Implement pagination, sorting, and filtering in the request body. Supported filters must include status and date range, and the organization boundary must be enforced before any pagination is applied. For employees without approval permission, restrict visibility to timesheets owned by the current employee account. For users with approval permission, return all submitted timesheets in the organization plus any own timesheets if that is part of the authorization policy.

Use the timesheet's week boundaries and status fields to filter results. Preserve the current organization scope across all pages. If the selected organization is missing or invalid, return an authorization/context error. If filter values are malformed or the date range is invalid, return a validation error. The response must be a paginated summary view optimized for list rendering, including the timesheet identity, owner, week range, status, and total hours derived from included timelogs.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summaries scoped to the selected organization.

requestBody.description: Timesheet list criteria including pagination, sorting, and filters for status and date range.

operations.description:
Create a draft weekly timesheet for the authenticated employee.

This operation creates the employee's weekly timesheet for a specific Monday-to-Sunday period in the currently selected organization. The new record is the editable draft version of the employee's weekly time collection and is intended for later submission, approval, or rejection in the timesheet workflow.

When a draft is created, the service must ensure it belongs to the authenticated employee's organization context, uses valid weekly boundaries, and does not duplicate an existing timesheet for the same employee and week. If the implementation supports automatic draft population, the draft should include the employee's timelogs for that week so the employee can review them before submission.

If the employee-week pair already exists, or if the requested week is invalid, the server must reject the request with the appropriate validation or conflict error. The response returns the created draft timesheet record.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Resolve the authenticated member's employee record in the selected organization context.
Validate that the requester is an active employee in that organization; deactivated employees must be rejected because they cannot submit or manage time.
Validate the requested timesheet week so that week_start_date is Monday and week_end_date is Sunday, and the range belongs to a single weekly period.
Check the unique constraint on (erp_hrm_time_employee_id, week_start_date) before insert. If a record already exists for that employee/week, return a conflict error.
Create the timesheet row with status set to draft and persist the employee ownership and week boundaries. The schema includes reviewed fields, rejection reason, and timestamps; set review-related fields to null on creation.
After creation, initialize the draft composition behavior required by the product rules: the employee should later be able to add or remove timelogs from the draft. Do not silently attach timelogs here unless the lower layer explicitly implements that as part of creation logic; if automatic inclusion is supported by the service, it must query the employee's timelogs for the target week within the same organization and insert join rows transactionally.
Enforce organization isolation using the employee's organization membership and the selected organization context; never allow cross-organization timesheet creation. Return the full created entity and surface validation, not-found, forbidden, and conflict errors as appropriate.

responseBody.description: The created draft weekly timesheet.

requestBody.description: Draft timesheet creation details for the target week.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timesheet for the currently selected organization.

This operation returns the full weekly timesheet record for one employee, including its week boundaries, status, total hours, submission and review metadata, and the timelogs that belong to that sheet. Timesheets are employee-owned records, so the response reflects the owning employee’s weekly time record and is suitable for detailed review screens, approval workflows, and employee self-service pages.

Access is limited to the selected organization. Employees may retrieve their own timesheets, and users with timesheet approval permission may retrieve submitted timesheets within the same organization. If the timesheet belongs to another organization, is not accessible in the current organization context, or the caller lacks permission, the request must fail with an authorization or not-found style error depending on the platform’s access policy.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the timesheet by its identifier with an organization-scoped query.
Verify that the timesheet belongs to the currently selected organization before returning it.
Join or separately load the owning employee and included timelogs so the response can expose the complete weekly record.
Apply access control rules: the owner can view their own timesheet; users with approval permission can view submitted timesheets in the same organization.
Reject access when the record is outside the active organization context or the caller is not permitted to view it.
Include the timesheet total hours as stored or derived from the included timelogs, ensuring the returned value matches the approved or current draft contents according to the timesheet state.
If the identifier does not resolve to a timesheet in the active organization, return a not found response.

responseBody.description: The full timesheet record for the requested week, including ownership, status, review metadata, and included timelogs.

parameters.description: The identifier of the timesheet to retrieve.
parameters.name: timesheetId

operations.description:
Update a weekly timesheet record for the selected organization.

This operation is used to modify a timesheet that belongs to a single employee and represents one Monday-to-Sunday work week. The timesheet stores the owning employee, the review metadata, the week boundaries, the lifecycle status, and the rejection reason when a submission is rejected. The included timelogs are maintained through the timesheet-timelog relation, so this operation updates the timesheet record itself while preserving the linked time entries.

Employees may use this operation to adjust their own draft or rejected timesheets within the currently selected organization. Approvers may use it as part of the review workflow to record review outcomes and related timestamps. The service must enforce organization isolation, verify that the target timesheet belongs to the active organization, and reject attempts to modify a timesheet from another organization. It must also enforce the business rules for timesheet state transitions and prevent invalid edits to submitted or approved records outside the allowed workflow.

If the timesheet is rejected, the rejection reason should be persisted on the record. If review metadata is changed, the service must keep the review timestamps and reviewer association consistent with the new state. Any invalid status transition, missing required review data, or unauthorized update must result in a validation or permission error.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by id with organization scope enforcement through the owning employee relation. Reject the request if the timesheet does not belong to the selected organization or the current user lacks access.

Allow updates only for fields supported by the timesheet model: week_start_date, week_end_date, status, submitted_at, reviewed_at, reviewed_by_member_id, and rejection_reason. Preserve id, employee ownership, and linked timesheet-timelog associations. Do not allow changing the owner through this endpoint.

Validate that week_start_date is Monday and week_end_date is Sunday, and that the week range remains coherent. Enforce the uniqueness rule for one timesheet per employee per week. If the week is changed, ensure no conflicting timesheet exists for that employee and week.

Enforce workflow rules based on status:
- Draft and rejected timesheets may be updated by their owner in the selected organization.
- Submitted and approved timesheets must not be arbitrarily modified; only review-related updates should be accepted when performed through the appropriate approval workflow.
- Rejection reason is required when setting the status to rejected.
- reviewed_at and reviewed_by_member_id must be consistent when approval or rejection is recorded.

Persist updates in a transaction. If state changes affect downstream totals, recompute derived total hours from the linked timelogs when serializing the response. Return not found for missing records, forbidden for cross-organization or unauthorized access, and conflict for duplicate weekly ownership or invalid workflow transitions.

responseBody.description: The updated timesheet record with its current ownership, status, review metadata, and week boundaries.

parameters.description: Timesheet identifier in UUID format within the selected organization scope.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Fields to update on the timesheet, including week boundaries and workflow metadata used by the approval process.

prerequisites.description: A weekly timesheet must exist before it can be updated.

operations.description:
Update the timelog membership of a weekly timesheet.

This operation lets an employee adjust which timelogs are included in a timesheet for a specific week. It supports the self-service workflow for draft and rejected timesheets, where the owner can add or remove work entries before resubmitting. The total hours for the timesheet are derived from the timelogs currently included in it, so the resulting composition directly affects the recorded summary for that week.

The timesheet must belong to the current organization context, and the caller must either own the timesheet or have a higher-privilege role that is allowed to manage timesheet contents. The system must reject changes when the timesheet is not in draft or rejected status, when the timesheet belongs to another employee, or when any selected timelog is locked because it is included in an approved timesheet. Changes must also preserve the weekly scope of the timesheet and avoid introducing timelogs from another organization or from outside the target employee's access scope.

Validation errors should explain missing or invalid timelog references, attempts to modify a forbidden timesheet status, and conflicts caused by locked timelogs or organization mismatch. After a successful update, the response should return a paginated timesheet summary so clients can refresh the total hours and included-entry state immediately.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by timesheetId within the authenticated member's selected organization context.
Verify that the timesheet exists and that the caller is allowed to edit its composition: the timesheet must belong to the caller's own employee record for self-service, or the caller must possess elevated organization permission that explicitly allows timesheet management. Reject access if the timesheet belongs to another organization.

Allow modifications only when the timesheet status is draft or rejected. If the timesheet is submitted or approved, return a business rule violation. If the timesheet is rejected, keep it editable and update its composition in place.

Process the request body as a composition diff for included timelogs. For each timelog to add, verify that it belongs to the same organization, belongs to the same employee as the timesheet owner, and falls within the same weekly range as the target timesheet. Prevent adding timelogs that are already locked because they are part of an approved timesheet. For each timelog to remove, verify it is currently attached to the timesheet.

Use a transaction to synchronize the timesheet-timelog join table. Insert new links and delete removed links as needed. Recalculate total hours from the current included timelogs after the change, using the stored duration values from the linked timelogs. Preserve approved-timesheet locks on unrelated timelogs and never mutate locked timelogs through this operation.

If the request produces an empty timesheet after removing entries, allow it only when the business rules permit an empty draft or rejected timesheet; otherwise reject according to the timesheet submission rules. Return a refreshed paginated timesheet summary with its updated included timelog composition and total hours. Ensure errors are specific for not found, forbidden, invalid state, invalid timelog ownership, and locked timelog conflicts.

responseBody.description: The paginated updated timesheet summary after timelog composition changes have been applied.

parameters.description: Timesheet identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Timelog add/remove instructions for updating the contents of a weekly timesheet.

operations.description:
Attach a timelog to a weekly timesheet for composition of the employee's time submission.

This operation creates a new association between the specified timesheet and an existing timelog. The timesheet must belong to the current organization context and must be owned by the same employee as the timelog. The timesheet-timelog link is stored in the join table, while the timelog record itself remains unchanged.

The association is intended for draft timesheets. The service must reject attempts to add timelogs to a timesheet that is already submitted or approved, and it must prevent duplicate links for the same timesheet and timelog pair. When the timelog is already included in the timesheet, the request should fail with a conflict-style validation error rather than creating a duplicate row.

Because timesheets are employee-owned and weekly scoped, the implementation must verify that the timelog falls within the same employee and week context as the target timesheet. If the timesheet is rejected but has been returned to draft, the employee may recompose it by adding or removing timelogs again.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Load the target timesheet by id within the active organization context and confirm it belongs to the authenticated employee unless the caller has elevated time management privileges. Reject if the timesheet does not exist or is outside the organization scope.

Validate that the target timesheet is in draft status. Do not allow adding timelogs to submitted or approved timesheets. If the business flow allows rejected timesheets to be returned to draft, treat them as draft for this operation only after they are reopened into draft state.

Load the referenced timelog from the request body and verify it exists, belongs to the same organization, and is owned by the same employee as the timesheet. Also verify the timelog work_date falls within the timesheet week range when the domain rules require weekly consistency.

Before insert, check the join table for an existing row with the same timesheet id and timelog id. If one exists, return a conflict-style validation error. Insert a new erp_hrm_time_timesheet_timelogs row with a generated UUID and current timestamps. No mutation is required on the timelog row itself.

After insert, recompute or refresh the timesheet total-hours projection if the implementation maintains one in the service layer or derived response. The total hours should reflect the sum of all included timelogs. Return the created association or the updated timesheet view according to the project DTO conventions. Ensure authorization and org-context checks happen before any data mutation.

responseBody.description: The newly created timesheet-to-timelog association.

parameters.description: Identifier of the timesheet that will receive the timelog.
parameters.name: timesheetId

requestBody.description: Identifies the existing timelog to attach to the timesheet.

prerequisites.description: A weekly timesheet must already exist for the employee before a timelog can be attached to it.
The timelog to be attached must already exist before the timesheet-timelog association can be created.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single timelog entry that belongs to a specific weekly timesheet.

This operation returns the association record that links one timesheet to one timelog, allowing clients to inspect which work entry is included in the weekly submission context. The timesheet is owned by exactly one employee, and only that employee or an authorized reviewer should be able to access the record within the selected organization context.

The response is intended for timesheet drafting, review, and audit workflows. It preserves the normalized timelog storage model by exposing the join row rather than duplicating the underlying timelog data. If the timesheet or the linked timelog cannot be found, or if the association does not belong to the specified timesheet, the service should return a not-found response.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Load the timesheet_timelogs row by its primary key and verify that it belongs to the provided timesheetId path parameter.

Validate organization scope through the parent timesheet and ensure the requester has permission to view the owning employee's timesheet or has approval access for submitted timesheets. Because the association row is normalized data, do not fetch unrelated timelog collections or attempt to infer the join through the timelog table alone.

If the row does not exist, is deleted, or does not belong to the specified timesheet, return 404. If organization context is missing or the requester lacks access, return the appropriate authorization error. Do not expose cross-organization data.

responseBody.description: The timesheet-to-timelog association within the requested weekly timesheet.

parameters.description: Identifier of the parent timesheet.
parameters.name: timesheetId

parameters.description: Identifier of the timesheet-timelog association row.
parameters.name: timesheetTimelogId

operations.description:
Remove a timelog from a weekly timesheet.

This operation deletes the association between a specific timesheet and a specific timelog. It does not delete the underlying timelog record; it only removes that timelog from the weekly submission container so the employee can adjust a draft timesheet before submission.

The timesheet must belong to the current organization context and the caller must have access to the owning employee's data. The association can be removed only while the timesheet is still editable. If the timesheet has already been approved, or if business rules prevent modification of the included timelog, the request must be rejected.

If the requested association does not exist, or if the timelog does not belong to the given timesheet, the operation must fail with a not-found style error. The implementation should use the timesheet and timelog identifiers together to locate the join row in erp_hrm_time_timesheet_timelogs and remove that row atomically.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Load the join row from erp_hrm_time_timesheet_timelogs using the parent timesheet ID and the child timelog association ID from the path. Verify that the join row belongs to the target timesheet and that the timesheet belongs to the caller's current organization scope.

Before deletion, check the parent timesheet status. Reject the request when the timesheet is approved, because approved timesheets lock included timelogs. Also reject when the association is missing, when the association belongs to a different timesheet, or when the caller lacks permission to edit the timesheet owner’s data.

Perform the deletion in a transaction. Delete only the join row; do not delete the timelog itself. Return the deleted association representation if the service pattern requires a body on DELETE, otherwise return no content. Preserve referential integrity and let cascading behavior remain limited to the association row only. Ensure the operation is idempotent from the client perspective by returning not-found on repeated removal attempts.

parameters.description: The timesheet identifier within the current organization context.
parameters.name: timesheetId

parameters.description: The timelog association identifier within the specified timesheet.
